name: smoke-by-link
title: The Smoke Script, Found by Link
kicker: Jenkins answers back · ARTIE follows what the build offers
html:
The Smoke Script, Found by Link

Jenkins Tells the CI Service

Its notification plugin posts each build event; the CI service answers ARTIE’s reply, signed, linking the build.

The Build Links What It Made

ci:deployment: where it runs. ci:smoke-test: the scenarios it shipped with.

ARTIE Follows, Then Runs

Neither address is in the script. Both came in the answer.

From the kept script 
- enter: ${jenkins}
  steps:
    - ask: ci:build
      fields:
        commit: ${merged.merge_commit_sha}
      reply: build
- once-answered:
    reply: build
    steps:
      - follow: hr:in-reply-to
        then:
          - run-script: ci:smoke-test
            on-link: ci:deployment
            as: smoke
say: When Jenkins finishes, it doesn't call ARTIE directly. Its notification plugin tells the CI service, and the CI service answers ARTIE's reply, signed, with a link to the build. ARTIE follows that link. A build that succeeded links two things: where it was deployed, ci:deployment, and the smoke scenarios it shipped with, ci:smoke-test, archived as an artifact of that very build. ARTIE runs the smoke script against the deployment. Neither address was in the kept script; both came in the answer. So a new build, on a new port, with new smoke scenarios, needs no change to the release script at all.
